GOAL: pick ONE mechanism that (a) satisfies the 5-part scope contract, (b) is consistent with the round-one/round-two negative results, (c) is not one of the already-rejected families (Poincare-Frechet successor codebook, CURVCTRL-SID per-level curvature, BRad-RQ behaviour-ranked radial assignment, BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ, TSG-SID, concentration-scaled geodesic step toward a successor barycentre (round two)).
WHAT I READ / USED: the round-three brief's three pieces of evidence: (i) prefix capacity separates the runs (L3 2201 -> 0.0544 vs L3 1298 -> 0.0517, baseline ~0.0679), every mechanism so far merged prefixes; (ii) behaviour-CONTRAST predicts recall (+0.7104), Gromov-delta and ancestor-depth weightings hurt (-0.12, -0.075), the radial term is group compactness not hierarchy; (iii) curvature is a gauge, and objectives minimised at the ball origin collapse the encoder; (iv) behaviour must reach the TOKENS; (v) level count and codebook sizes are Stage-2 architecture, open to change inside the 0.15 s/epoch budget.

Per-item rotation of the level-3 residual query inside the tangent plane spanned by the radial direction and the item's successor-contrast direction; the rotation angle is the holonomy (= geodesic-triangle area) of the hyperbolic triangle (origin, prefix point, unit contrast probe), so it is 0 in the flat limit and 0 when the behaviour direction is switched off. It also adds capacity exactly where the evidence says capacity was lost: level 2 and level 3 go from 256 to 512 codewords, with the 3-token SID length and the frozen Stage-3 protocol untouched.
